problem: Learned image-goal navigation policies (IL, RL, modular) capture semantic priors for exploration but ignore the geometric structure of the last mile, once the goal is in view. They are sample-inefficient or biased (e.g., toward zero heading) there, and one-sided explore-to-exploit hand-offs are too optimistic and cannot recover from errors.
motivation: Last-mile errors are a prominent failure mode: a stop-budget study shows NRNS success rising from about 28% to 51% with just one extra stop. Once the goal is visible, relative pose can be solved with classical geometry (keypoints + depth + PnP) instead of learned from demonstrations. Learned policies also inherit a training heading bias (72.2% of training headings within ±15° versus 39.4% at test).
key_idea: Plug a geometric last-mile module (SuperPoint/SuperGlue correspondences, depth lifting, ePnP+RANSAC pose to get goal distance and heading) into any image-goal exploration policy via symmetric explore-to-exploit and exploit-to-explore switches.
insight: Structure at the last mile beats learning it: SLING beats a DDPPO trained 400M steps for last-mile navigation (54.8 vs 44.3 success) and adds gains to every explorer tested. Ablations show both switches matter: replacing the geometric switch with the MLP switch and removing recovery drops the OVRL-based success from 54.8 to 37.9. Neural features help, and the heading-distribution analysis shows why: SLING matches test heading distribution better (Wasserstein 0.0034 vs NRNS 0.0134). Oracle experiments show that with perfect goal discovery SLING reaches 86.2 vs 67.7.
method: Goal-discovery (explore) policies: Straight heuristic, NRNS topological-graph, DDPPO, OVRL, and an Oracle-GD privileged NRNS variant serve as pluggable explorers
Feature extraction and matching: SuperPoint keypoints/descriptors on the agent RGB and the goal image, matched by SuperGlue (attention GNN with optimal transport)

2D to 3D lifting and PnP: matched agent keypoints are lifted with depth and intrinsics, then ePnP + RANSAC minimizes reprojection error to give R, t; distance = ||t||, heading from t and the optical axis
Local policy: distance and heading become a waypoint; a local metric map with fast marching handles obstacle avoidance, as in NRNS/Active Neural SLAM
Explore→exploit switch: triggers when the number of matches exceeds a threshold (50 for NRNS/Straight, 20 for OVRL)
Exploit→explore switch: returns control to exploration if PnP fails or the predicted distance exceeds 4 m, enabling recovery
Real-robot deployment: TerraSentia with RealSense D435i, ORB-SLAM2 pose, NMPC control, NRNS trained on RealEstate10K as the explorer

setting.backbone: Modular: pretrained SuperPoint + SuperGlue with classical ePnP/RANSAC, on top of explorer policies (Straight, NRNS, DDPPO, OVRL, Oracle-GD)
setting.training_data: SLING module needs no navigation training (pretrained SuperPoint/SuperGlue, hand-set thresholds); explorers are trained as in prior work (DDPPO/OVRL 500M steps on Gibson/MP3D episodes, NRNS on offline trajectories); DDPPO-LMN baseline trained 400M steps
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB + depth + agent pose, plus RGB image-goal (640x480 at 120° FoV for NRNS/Straight; 128x128 at 90° for OVRL/DDPPO)
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level: move forward, turn left, turn right, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson, MP3D image-goal benchmark of NRNS) + real world
setting.privileged: none for the main method (depth and pose sensors assumed); Oracle-GD, Oracle-Det and Oracle-PT ablations use ground truth

numbers.eval_set_note: Gibson-curved fold (NRNS benchmark), overall over easy/medium/hard
numbers.extra: 128x128 images, 90° FoV, non-panoramic; pose and depth sensors assumed

numbers.backbone: OVRL retrained on panoramic images + SLING on front-facing crop

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 real scenes, 120 trajectories total (easy episodes, goals 1.5-3 m)
3 real scenes, 120 trajectories total (hard episodes, goals 5-10 m)

numbers_note: The split is the benchmark's fold (test episodes). Difficulty-wise results (easy/medium/hard) are in the tables but not listed here. The multi-seed table gives SLING+OVRL-GD 56.3±2.4 SR / 37.3±0.7 SPL on Gibson-curved.
results: SLING + OVRL reaches 54.8% success / 37.3 SPL on Gibson-curved, +21.8 over ZER (33.0) and +9.2 over OVRL (45.6). It improves every explorer tested (DDPPO +22.2, NRNS +21.8) across Gibson/MP3D and straight/curved folds, and on a real robot success rises from 40.0 to 56.6 (easy) and 3.3 to 20.0 (hard) over NRNS.
limitations: Depends on keypoint matching quality and needs depth and pose sensors
Extra hyperparameters (match count and distance thresholds) tuned per image size
Uses only the current observation for one-shot pose prediction (no temporal smoothing); needs the goal to be directly visible with enough overlap
